reasons.resultError: The agent ended with an error ({{subtype}}): {{detail}}
reasons.exitedWithoutResult: Claude Code exited with code {{exitCode}} without reporting a result.

reasons.noGithubRemote: This project's repo isn't on GitHub, so there's nowhere to open a pull request.
reasons.githubAccountMissing: Choose which GitHub account this project uses.

reasons.nothingToDeliver: There's nothing to deliver: no step changed any files.

reasons.setupFailed: Preparing the project failed with code {{exitCode}}.
reasons.noStructuredOutput: It finished without the answer it was asked for.

reasons.brainFull: The Brain is full. Retire something first, and then accept this.
reasons.defaultWorkflowMissing: The workflow this project uses by default no longer exists. Choose another one in Settings.
reasons.projectHasOpenRuns: This project can't be removed yet, because “{{title}}” hasn't finished. Finish it or abandon it first.

reasons.specNotUsable: It couldn't write this within what Keel can show you, even after being asked to fix it: {{problems}}.
reasons.invalidAnswer: That answer doesn't belong to these questions.
reasons.sendBackNeedsInstructions: To send it back, say what should change.
reasons.nothingToSendBackTo: Nothing before this approval can do the work again.
reasons.nothingSkippedToRun: Nothing was skipped for being a small change, so there's nothing to run.

reasons.partsNotOpened: You approved it, but Keel couldn't put each project's part on the board: {{detail}}. Try again once that's fixed.

reasons.readCopyFailed: Keel couldn't get a copy of {{project}} to read: {{detail}}. Try again once it can be reached.

run.decideClosed: Nothing. The pull request was closed without merging.
run.decideRejected: Nothing. You rejected this, and your reason will reach this project's next runs.
run.approvalTitle: Should this become a pull request?
run.agreementBody: Approving puts a card on the board for each part, in this order. Each one starts once the one before it has a pull request. Nothing changes in any project until then.
run.agreementApproveHint: Each part runs its project's usual workflow, and a person approves it before its pull request.
run.approvalBody: Nothing has left your Mac yet.
run.approvalEmptyBody: There's nothing to turn into a pull request.
run.approvalNote: Why you're rejecting, or an optional note if you approve
run.approvalNoteHint: Either way, later agents on this project get it as a decision to follow.
run.approvalNotePrHint: If you approve, it also goes in the pull request.
run.approvalRejectHint: Ends this run. Nothing leaves your Mac.
run.approvalRejectNeedsReason: Say why above first, so later agents learn from it.
run.approvalApproveHint: Pushes a keel/* branch and opens a draft pull request. Merges nothing.
run.approvalLaterHint: Runs the next steps, which can end in a draft pull request. Merges nothing.
run.approvalNoPushHint: This workflow doesn't open a pull request, so nothing gets pushed.
run.approvalCloseHint: It stays on record as rejected. Nothing leaves your Mac.
run.approvalReadAsked: Read all of what was asked
run.approvalCheckFailed: Keel ran `{{command}}` and it didn't pass.
run.approvalNoCheck: Keel ran no check of its own, so if the agent says the tests pass, that's its word.
run.approvalReviewsOnlyRead: The reviews only read the code. They didn't run it.
run.workflowWarning: This change edits `.github/workflows`. Those files can run with the repo's secrets as soon as the branch is pushed. Read them first.
run.secretWarning: This change might hold a secret. Masking only hides it here: approving pushes it with the branch. Check the changes first.
run.secretWarningLocal: This change might hold a secret. Masking only hides it here: it's still in the run's code. Check the changes first.
run.checkFailedSummary: A check failed, so this didn't go further.
run.decideReworkLimit: Choose above: one more round, your approval, or leave it.

run.proposalsHint: If you accept one, every agent on this project gets it from now on.
run.mapWritten: It wrote a map with {{count}} lines.
run.decideMap: Nothing. Read it in the Brain, and retire any line that's wrong.

run.questionsBody: Choose what should happen. Where an option is recommended, it's already selected.
run.questionsLastRound: This is the last round of questions. If it asks anything after this, Keel takes the recommended option, or asks you once more where there's none.
run.questionsExtraRound: An extra round, because something has no recommended option. If it keeps asking after this, Keel stops the run.
run.questionOtherNeeded: Write your answer, or choose one of the options.
run.questionNoneRecommended: None recommended: neither the code nor the request says. It's yours to decide.
run.questionRememberHint: An answer only counts for this run unless you remember it. You can retire remembered ones in the Brain.
run.questionsUseRecommendedHint: Free and instant: no agent runs.
run.questionsUseRecommendedNone: Not here: a question has no recommended option.
run.questionsAnswerHint: The agent goes on with your answers, which uses your Claude usage.
run.questionsAnswerSame: Choose another option to answer differently.
run.questionsAnswerEach: Answer every question to go on.
run.questionsCancelHint: Ends this run. If it has a card on the board, the card goes back to the backlog.
run.decidedKeelTook: The rounds of questions ran out, so Keel stopped asking and took the recommended option.
run.sendBackHint: It goes back to the step that does the work, without starting over, and comes back to you here. Your words stay in this run.

settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHint: Applies to the app and to what agents write from now on.
settings.githubHint: Keel uses this account for this project only, and never changes the one active in your terminal.
settings.githubNoRepo: This project's repo isn't on GitHub.
settings.githubUnprotected: {{branch}} isn't protected, so anyone with write access can push to it directly. Keel never does, but a protected branch adds a safeguard.
settings.githubScopes: This account's token also has {{scopes}}. Keel doesn't need them and can't reduce them. A dedicated account limits what could go wrong.
settings.githubNoAccess: {{account}} can't see this repo. Give it access on GitHub, then accept the invitation with that account.
settings.githubReadOnly: {{account}} can see this repo but can't push to it, so Keel couldn't open a pull request. Give it write access on GitHub.
settings.githubAccessHint: These open in your browser. To give access, use a session that administers the repo. To accept, use {{account}}'s session.
settings.githubLinksHint: Managing access opens GitHub in your browser, and only someone who administers the repo sees that page. Connecting an account opens Terminal, because gh keeps the session, not Keel.
settings.githubConnectHint: This opens Terminal, because gh keeps the session, not Keel.
settings.checkCommandHint: Runs after the builder, in a sandbox with no network and no access to your home folder. Exit code 0 passes.
settings.domainsHint: One per line. Nothing else is reachable.
settings.readPathsHint: One per line, such as ~/.nvm. Your home folder is hidden otherwise.
settings.sensitive: Files too sensitive for a small change
settings.sensitiveHint: One pattern per line, such as billing/ or *.proto. A change that touches one gets the full review. These always count: .github/ and other CI, build and dependency files, test settings, migrations, SQL schema, sign-in and permissions, secrets, environment files and lock files.
settings.servicesHint: What this project's commands need, such as a test database. Keel runs them outside the sandbox while a step uses them, and commands reach them only through a Unix socket.
settings.serviceTypeBridge: Forwards to a port on this Mac, such as a database in Docker.
settings.serviceTypeCommand: Keel starts this command, which must listen on $KEEL_SOCKET.
settings.envHint: One per line, as NAME=value. In a value, socketDir and socket with the service name, between double braces, become that service's paths. They're saved in plain text and recorded in the audit log, so don't put secrets here.
settings.envInvalid: This line needs the form NAME=value: “{{line}}”.
settings.setupCommandHint: Installs what the project needs, once per run, before any agent. It can reach the internet, but not your home folder or anything else on this Mac. Your repo's own scripts may run here.
settings.maxAgentsHint: Applies to the whole app, not to each project. More agents use your Claude plan faster.
settings.defaultWorkflowHint: What a card on the board runs when you move it to Todo.
settings.defaultWorkflowGone: A workflow that no longer exists

invalidSettings.servicePort: Choose a port for the service.
invalidSettings.envName: A variable name uses capital letters, numbers and underscores: “{{value}}”.
invalidSettings.envReserved: Keel controls “{{value}}”, or it could carry a credential, so a project can't set it.
invalidSettings.sensitivePaths: “{{value}}” can't be read as a file pattern.

invalidWorkflow.empty: A workflow needs at least one step.
invalidWorkflow.badId: “{{step}}” can't be a step's name. Use letters, numbers and hyphens.
invalidWorkflow.badPath: “{{step}}” has a file pattern that can't be read.
invalidWorkflow.reviewerMustReadOnly: “{{step}}” judges the work, so it can only read.
invalidWorkflow.parallelMustReadOnly: “{{step}}” is in a group that runs at once, and they share one copy of the code, so it can only read.
invalidWorkflow.reworkTarget: “{{step}}” sends work back to a step that has to come before it.
invalidWorkflow.tooManyRounds: “{{step}}” can send work back 5 times at most.
invalidWorkflow.deliverNeedsApproval: “{{step}}” opens a pull request, so a person has to approve in a step before it.
invalidWorkflow.learnerNotLast: “{{step}}” proposes what the run taught, so it has to be the last step.
invalidWorkflow.groupRole: “{{step}}” can't run in a group. Only steps that do the work or review it can.
invalidWorkflow.verifierNeedsSpecifier: “{{step}}” goes through what has to be true, so a step that works out the change has to come before it.
invalidWorkflow.whenBeforeBuild: “{{step}}” depends on how big the change is, so it has to come after the first step that builds. Before that there's no change to look at.

workflows.title: Workflows
workflows.subtitle: The steps a run goes through, with the model for each one.
workflows.builtinNote: This one comes with Keel. Saving makes a copy for this project.
workflows.name: Name
workflows.approvalHint: The run waits here for you, for as long as it takes.
workflows.deliverHint: Keel pushes a branch and opens a draft. It never merges.
workflows.pathsHint: Patterns separated by commas, such as **/*.tsx. Empty means it always runs.
workflows.whenNotSmall: Only if the change isn't small
workflows.whenHint: Keel decides that from the real change: what was asked, a check that passed, who wrote the issue, nothing sensitive and under 400 lines. It goes after the first step that builds, and a person still approves.
workflows.promptHint: You can use {{tokens}}, where spec is a step's name.
workflows.draftNote: It can't run until you save it. What gets saved is what you see here, with your changes, as a new workflow.
workflows.draftPrompts: Each step in the diagram has its prompt. Open them before you save.
workflows.draftBuilders: Agents that can change files and run commands
workflows.draftAfterApproval_one: {{steps}} runs after your approval and before the pull request. Whatever it changes goes up without you seeing it. To see it first, move your approval after it.
workflows.draftAfterApproval_other: {{steps}} run after your approval and before the pull request. Whatever they change goes up without you seeing it. To see it first, move your approval after them.

results.hint: How the runs of each workflow in this project have gone. Runs from before Keel kept track of this aren't counted.

results.criteriaUnverified: What had to be true: not verified

onboarding.title: Welcome to Keel
onboarding.intro: Keel runs Claude Code agents on private copies of your repos, step by step, and shows what each one did. A person always decides what ships.
onboarding.githubReady: Signed in as {{accounts}}. Each project picks its own account.
onboarding.githubMissing: The built-in workflows end in a draft pull request, so they won't start without it. Without it, only a single step or a custom workflow with no delivery can run.
onboarding.githubSignedOut: It's installed, but nobody is signed in. Without an account, only a single step or a custom workflow with no delivery can run.
onboarding.projectHint: Pick a folder with a git repo. Keel works on a copy and never changes yours. An agent will read it to write its map, using your Claude Code plan.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.hint: Lets an assistant like Claude Code see your projects and start runs on this Mac, and you watch them here. Only this Mac can reach it, and it's off until you turn it on.
mcp.limits: If you allow it, it can send work back, try a step again and close the runs it started. It can't approve or reject a step, answer the questions a step asks, merge, change settings, save a workflow or accept anything into the Brain. Those stay with you, here. A workflow it proposes waits for you on Workflows, and can't run until you save it. A project it proposes isn't added until you add it.
mcp.portInUse: Port {{port}} is in use by another program. Choose another one.
mcp.connected: Connected. New Claude Code sessions see it on their own. In one that's already open, run /mcp.
mcp.canRun: Can start and stop runs, and propose workflows and projects
mcp.canSteer: Can give feedback: send work back, try again and close its runs
mcp.canSteerNeedsRun: Turn on the one above first.
mcp.maxOpenRunsHint: up to {{max}}, counting those waiting for you
mcp.tokenOnce: This is the only time Keel shows this token. Copy it now.

projects.proposalBanner_other: {{client}} proposes adding {{name}}, and {{more}} more are waiting
projects.proposalNoGithub: This folder has no GitHub remote
projects.proposalMap: Adding it starts an agent that reads the repository to write its map, on your Claude usage. Then you choose its GitHub account and commands.
projects.proposalReturning: It was in Keel before. It comes back with its history, and no new map.
projects.proposalGone: This folder isn't a git repository with commits anymore, so all you can do is discard it.

setup.restored: It was removed from Keel before. Its runs, its audit record, its Brain and its cards are as they were, and any cards in Todo start now.
setup.several: More than one of your accounts can push to {{repo}}. Choose which one this project uses.
setup.noPusher: None of your accounts can push to {{repo}}, so Keel couldn't open a pull request.
setup.noRemote: This repo isn't on GitHub, so runs here can't open a pull request. Once it's published, open this again and Keel will notice.
setup.noGh: GitHub CLI (gh) isn't installed, so Keel has no way to open a pull request for this project.
setup.noAccount: Nobody is signed in to GitHub CLI, so Keel has no account to open a pull request with.
setup.passed: It passed. Nothing is saved until you save.
setup.notFound: That command couldn't be found in the sandbox, which can't see your home folder. If it's installed there, add its folder under “Other folders agents can read” in Settings.
setup.noGuess: Keel couldn't tell how this project tests itself, so these are empty.
setup.noCheckNote: Without a check, runs go out unverified.
setup.mapStarted: Keel is reading this project to write its map.
setup.mapSignedOut: You aren't signed in to Claude Code, so Keel can't write this project's map yet. Sign in, then start it from the Brain.
setup.mapFailed: Keel couldn't start this project's map. {{reason}} You can start it from the Brain.

remove.title: Remove {{name}} from Keel?
remove.does: It leaves your project lists, and nothing can start on it, from here or from an assistant. Its cards stay where they are, and none of them start.
remove.doesNot: Nothing is deleted. Your folder isn't touched. Its runs stay on Home as history, and its audit record and Brain stay in Keel.
remove.comeBack: To bring it back with all of that, add the same folder again. Any cards it has in Todo start then, because you asked for them.

specProblems.tooManyChanges: it lists {{count}} changes, and the limit is {{limit}}
specProblems.tooManyLimits: it lists {{count}} things that must not change, and the limit is {{limit}}
specProblems.unreadable: what it wrote isn't in the form Keel asked for
specProblems.noSummary: it didn't say what will change
specProblems.summaryTooLong: the sentence saying what will change has {{chars}} characters, and the limit is {{limit}}
specProblems.noCriteria: it didn't say how to tell the change works
specProblems.tooManyCriteria: it lists {{count}} things that have to be true, and the limit is {{limit}}
specProblems.criterionTooLong: {{id}} has {{chars}} characters, and the limit is {{limit}}

specProblems.repeatedCriterion: two things that have to be true are both called {{id}}
specProblems.tooManyDecided: it lists {{count}} things it decided alone, and the limit is {{limit}}
specProblems.decidedTooLong: something it decided alone has {{chars}} characters, and the limit is {{limit}}
specProblems.tooManyQuestions: it has {{count}} questions for you, and the limit is {{limit}}
specProblems.questionTooLong: question {{id}} has {{chars}} characters, and the limit is {{limit}}
specProblems.wrongNumberOfOptions: question {{id}} has {{count}} options, and it needs {{min}} to {{max}}
specProblems.optionTooLong: an option of question {{id}} has {{chars}} characters, and the limit is {{limit}}
specProblems.repeatedOption: question {{id}} has empty or repeated options
specProblems.tooManyRecommended: question {{id}} has {{count}} recommended options, and it can have one at most
specProblems.noParts: it didn't say what changes in any of the projects
specProblems.tooManyParts: it changes {{count}} projects, and the limit is {{limit}}

specProblems.tooManyTogether: it lists {{count}} things to try together, and the limit is {{limit}}

invalidAnswers.unknownQuestion: That answer is for a question this step didn't ask.
invalidAnswers.optionNotOffered: That option isn't one of those on offer for question {{question}}.
invalidAnswers.emptyText: Write your answer to question {{question}}, or choose one of its options.

fits.small: Keel treated this as a small change: {{lines}} in {{files}}. It touches nothing sensitive, and the check passed.
fits.runNowHint: Nothing already built is done again, and this approval comes back when they finish.
fits.up: It went to full review because:
fits.summary: Keel treated this as a small change, so these didn't run: {{names}}.

why.keelChoseAnAnswer: after two rounds of questions, Keel took an option itself, so nobody really chose it
why.specNotSmall: whoever worked out the change didn't call it small
why.noCheck: this workflow has no check, so nothing proves it works
why.checkNotPassed: the check hasn't passed on the code as it is now
why.issueFromSomeoneElse: it comes from an issue by {{author}}, who isn't this project's account
why.issueFromUnknownAuthor: it comes from an issue, and it isn't known who wrote it
why.issueWithNoAccount: it comes from an issue, and this project has no GitHub account to compare its author with
why.startedByAssistant: {{client}} started it, so no person wrote what it asks
why.badSensitivePattern: this project's list of sensitive files has something Keel can't read: {{pattern}}
why.tooManyLines: it changes {{lines}} lines, and a small change stays under {{limit}}
why.filesWithoutLines: Keel can't tell how much changed in {{files}}
why.verifierFoundUnmet: something that had to be true isn't
why.verifierHasNotRun: nobody has checked yet that this code does what was asked
why.partOfJointChange: it's one part of a change across several projects, and the parts only work together
why.unknown: Keel found a reason it can't put in words here

risks.concurrency: things happening at the same time
risks.noRegressionTest: something no test would catch breaking again

short.partOfJointChange: part of a change across projects

joint.title: Change across several projects
joint.notAgreed: Not agreed yet. That happens on “{{title}}”, in {{project}}.
joint.agreedInGone: The card where it was agreed is no longer on the board.
joint.togetherHint: No part proves these on its own. Try them once every part is in place, and mark what works.
joint.stopWaitingHint: Lets this part start without the pull request of the one before it.
